title: meg-: megcsinál and the Idea of 'Completely Done'

sections.title: Turning an action into a finished job
sections.content: meg- is Hungarian's classic completive prefix. Glued onto a verb, it takes an action that could otherwise go on indefinitely and marks it as finished, wrapped up, completely done. csinál on its own just means 'do, make' in general — Mit csinálsz? asks 'What are you doing?' with no sense of whether it ever ends. Add meg-, and megcsinál means 'to get something done, to finish doing it' — one specific, definite job, now completely handled.

items.english: I'm doing something in the kitchen.

items.spanish: Anna megcsinálja a jelentést, és hazamegy.
items.english: Anna gets the report done, and goes home.

sections.content: csinálok valamit describes an ongoing, unspecified activity — you can't tell if or when it ends. megcsinálom a feladatot names one particular, definite task and says it's now completely finished — that's why meg- shows up together with the definite conjugation, just like befejez did in the last lesson.
